clips.m1: These three Shorts, and this whole video, were edited by an AI. I only dropped the files in a folder.
clips.m2: Example one. A phone recording of me talking. Claude cut it, added b-roll, captions, zooms and music. I never opened an editor.
clips.m3: Example two. A long video goes in, and a ready Short comes out. It finds the hook, tracks my face, and captions every word.
clips.m4: Example three. No camera at all. This video is just a script, a clone of my own voice, and an animation engine.
clips.m5: It's called the AI Video Editor, and it's free and open source. One command, slash ai dash video, asks what you have and what you want.
clips.m6: Installing takes one command. Clone the repo, and run install dot py with the yes flag. Or paste one prompt, and let Claude do it for you.
clips.m7: You approve every video before anything goes out. Then Claude asks which account, shows a dry run, and schedules it. Forty clips? One CSV. Nothing posts twice, and never to the wrong channel.
clips.m8: Everything here, the repo, the docs, and this video, was made completely by Claude. The narration is a clone of my own voice. The link is in the description.
clips.h1: An AI edited this Short. I never touched a timeline. I dropped one phone video in a folder. Claude cut it, captioned every word, added zooms and music, and checked every frame. One command: slash ai dash video. Free and open source. Link in the description.
clips.h2: Stop editing Shorts by hand. Drop your video in a folder, and say what you want. Claude edits it, you approve it, and it schedules itself. Free, open source, and made completely by Claude. Link in the description.
clips.h3: Forty videos. One spreadsheet. Zero duplicates. Fill in one CSV. Claude asks which account, shows a dry run, and only posts after you say go. YouTube publishes them for you. Free and open source. Link in the description.
